articles.title: Jon Watts to Direct Next ‘Star Wars’ Movie
articles.summary: A new “Star Wars” movie is currently in development with director Jon Watts attached. Watts is best known for directing the popular “Spider-Man” trilogy starring Tom Holland, which includes 2017’s Spider-Man: Homecoming,” 2019’s “Spider-Man: Far From Home,” and 2021’s “Spider-Man: No Way Home.”…
body: With the role, Watts joins a list of previous “Star Wars” directors that includes Irvin Kershner, Richard Marquand, J.J. Abrams, Rian Johnson and “Star Wars” creator George Lucas. Released in 2019, Abrams’ “Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker” is the most recent film in the franchise to debut theatrically.

As previously reported by Variety, Simon Kinberg will pen the script for the film. Kinberg is best known for being a writer, producer and director for the “X-Men” franchise, and was considered a surprising choice at the time of the announcement.

articles.title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Director Champions Franchise’s First R Rating as Sequel Rocks NYFF at World Premiere: ‘Censoring’ the Action ‘Was Not an Option’
articles.summary: “Godzilla Minus Zero” blew the roof off Alice Tully Hall during its rapturous world premiere screening at the New York Film Festival. The long-awaited sequel to 2023’s “Godzilla Minus One” earned rave first reactions from the press earlier in the day, and that adoration rolled right into the world…
body: Inside the world premiere screening, New York Film Festival director Dennis Lim acknowledged that the Godzilla franchise might not be the first thing people think of playing at a major film festival. And yet, “We thought it was about time to bring a giant monster movie here.”
Yamazaki took the stage to thunderous applause from the audience both before and after the screening, where he asked the crowd not to spoil any of the sequel’s many surprises on social media.

“You are the first to see this film,” the filmmaker said. “There are a lot of ‘Godzilla’ fans around the world, so let’s work together and do not do any spoilers. No spoilers, please! I am trusting all of you guys.”

Yamazaki also had the audience laughing while explaining how he never intended to create a sequel to “Godzilla Minus One.” Executives at Toho immediately started asking him about a follow-up movie once they saw the first cut of “Minus One,” a thought that made Yamazaki instantly nervous. It wasn’t until the movie opened in theaters and started to be celebrated around the world by audiences that the director realized a sequel would be a viable option.

articles.title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Review: Godzilla and King Ghidorah Battle to the Death in the Even Grander Follow-Up to ‘Godzilla Minus One’
articles.summary: Yamazaki, who rebooted the genre and took it to a new peak in the revelatory 2023 retro kaiju classic "Godzilla Minus One," works with a quality that none of the filmmakers of recent decades has summoned: a fairy-tale innocence, an immersion in the annihilating heavy-metal poetry of Godzilla — the…
body: The humanistic heroes of the first film return, and so does writer-director Takashi Yamazaki's awesome sense of monster action paintings in motion.

When you go to see a big visual-effects movie, like something from Marvel, the closing credits that roll on for 12 minutes will feature multiple armies of visual-effects teams (each digital company with its own general). I have no doubt that a formidable army worked on “Godzilla Minus Zero.” But it’s also a movie that features the highly unusual credit “VFX, written, and directed by Takashi Yamazaki.” That’s a sign of how much the movie’s visual effects emanate directly from the imagination of the filmmaker. He’s writing, he’s directing, and he’s orchestrating spectacular gargantuan action paintings of beasts in motion. He’s an artist of larger-than-life pop horror.

articles.title: Radio 2 presenter to take on 'greatest ever distance' in Children in Need challenge
articles.summary: Owain Wyn Evans will cycle almost 400 miles, setting off from Glasgow and finishing in Cardiff.
body: Radio presenter Owain Wyn Evans will cycle through all four UK nations to raise money for BBC Children in Need.
The five-day challenge will start on Monday, 9 November, and finish on Friday, 13 November - when the fundraiser will be broadcast.
The only member of the annual TV fundraiser's hosting team for 2026 to be revealed so far is fellow Welsh presenter, One Show host Alex Jones.
The BBC said Evans' challenge would be the "greatest ever distance" covered in a Radio 2 endeavour for the charity.

articles.title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Review: Monster Movie Genius Takashi Yamazaki Returns With a Crackling Kaiju Epic Every Bit as Exciting as Its Predecessor
articles.summary: This direct sequel to the 2023 global sensation picks up in 1949, as a makeshift family finds its domestic harmony again threatened by a rampaging creature’s path of destruction.
body: While the 1949 setting might be expected to make the aftermath of war recede into the past, it’s no less acutely felt here, with resonant moments touching on the complicated perceptions of the Japanese people toward America and the outsize impact on the rest of the world of its military industrial complex. World War II may be over, but its vicious cycle of loss, destruction and power-flexing continues.

At the risk of angering the spoiler police — a cue to stop reading now if you’d rather go in blind — the new film ushers in another legendary kaiju first seen in 1964. Promotional materials for the most part refer evasively to “a new threat,” but fan anticipation and advance media have pretty much let the badass three-headed dragon out of the bag.

Just as Japanese life appears to be returning to some kind of peacetime normalcy, with Godzilla exiled to the ocean depths and believed to have been killed in the previous movie, King Ghidorah comes swooping in with massive wings generating hurricane-force winds, ripping apart an entire town in the opening action.

articles.title: James Gray on Broader Takeaways From Personal Film ‘Paper Tiger’: “What Connects Us Is What Matters”
articles.summary: As the crime thriller had its North American premiere at the New York Film Festival, the director spoke about how he hoped the domestic drama's open-ended resolution allows the story to continue for the audience after the credits.
body: James Gray ‘s latest film Paper Tiger, like most of his work, draws from his personal and family history to tell a semi-fictionalized story of a Queens family in the 1980s that becomes entangled with the Russian mob, thanks to a moneymaking scheme pitched to patriarch Irwin ( Miles Teller ) by older brother Gary ( Adam Driver ).
Coming after semi-autobiographical coming-of-age drama Armageddon Time, the crime thriller, Gray says, is not a sequel and doesn’t hew as closely to his own experience.
In addition to the thrills, Gray told THR before the Paper Tiger premiere that he’s hopeful audiences recognize the power of interpersonal relationships in the domestic drama.

“I was trying to make a film in which the personal connection is everything, that love is everything,” Gray said. “Through that of course you want people to feel suspense and intensity and things that we love in a good drama, you hope. But then in the end, dare I use the word catharsis, what connects us is what matters. It’s almost a cautionary tale.”

articles.title: Robert Vaughn Played A Small Part In One Of The Worst Superhero Movies Ever Made
articles.summary: While his role on The Man from U.N.C.L.E. brought Robert Vaughn great success, the same cannot be said for his turn in this superhero movie misfire.
body: Everyone knows Robert Vaughn as the suave secret agent Napoleon Solo from the 1960s NBC series "The Man from U.N.C.L.E." But in 1983, he played the kind of villain Solo would have taken down with a wry smile and a cool insouciance. Indeed, the actor's character, Ross Webster, was a scheming industrialist who faced off against the Man of Steel in 1983's "Superman III." In retrospect, Vaughn probably would have preferred for Webster to be a quickly forgotten villain on his spy series, though, as "Superman III" turned out to be a bit of a dud, and that's putting it lightly.

articles.title: Mike Leigh’s ‘Tender Loving Care’ Sweeps San Sebastian Awards as ‘La Bola Negra,’ ‘NAZA’ Earn Audience Nods
articles.summary: Amanda Kernell's 'Brace Your Heart' won the Swedish-Sami filmmaker the Silver Shell for best director as the Spanish film fest wrapped up its 74th edition, the last for outgoing director Jose Luis Rebordinos.
body: Mike Leigh ’s dramatic comedy Tender Loving Care took home three top awards at Saturday night’s closing ceremony of the 74th annual edition of the San Sebastian International Film Festival, which ran Sept. 18-26, including the Golden Shell for best film and Silver Shell for Kate O’Flynn’s lead performance.
O’Flynn shared the award with Asta Kamma August for her work in Hans Petter Moland’s Growth of the Soil, which also took home best cinematography for DP Oskar Dahlsbakken.

The Silver Shell for best director went to Sweden’s Amanda Kernell for Brace Your Heart. She dedicated the prize to members of the Sami culture represented in her film about reindeer herders, a “living culture facing immense stress.” She highlighted “the importance that films can give voice to those without a voice and be this machine of empathy.”
The Special Jury Prize went to Ah Biao’s Border. Spain ’s Javier Cámara took home the Silver Shell for best supporting performance in Javier Ruiz Caldera’s 5 More Minutes.

articles.title: ‘Star Wars’: Jon Watts to Direct Next Movie for Lucasfilm
articles.summary: Simon Kinberg is writing the new trilogy that is said to be next episodes of the Skywalker Saga.
body: Even as Lucasfilm is deep in post-production on its next Star Wars movie, Star Wars: Starfighter, the next phase of a potential new Skywalker Saga is coming into focus.

Jon Watts, the director behind a trio of Tom Holland Spider-Man movies, is now attached to direct the first installment of the Simon Kinberg -penned trilogy. It is a return to the franchise for Watts, who previously co-created Star Wars series Skeleton Crew in 2024.
Sources say the project is still in development and has not yet been greenlit by parent company Disney, although it seems to be project the furthest along the development track after Starfighter.
Starfighter is being directed by Shawn Levy and stars Ryan Gosling. The movie is expected to hit theatres May 27, 2027, coinciding with the 50th anniversary of Star Wars.
